newsitem.title: USA: HORSE RACING-SILVER CHARM NAMED 6-5 FAVORITE FOR BELMONT STAKES.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-SILVER CHARM NAMED 6-5 FAVORITE FOR BELMONT STAKES.

text.p: Kentucky Derby and Preakness winner Silver Charm was listed as the 6-5 early betting favourite on Thursday to win Saturday's Belmont Stakes and complete a sweep of thoroughbred racing's Triple Crown.
Silver Charm, winner of the Kentucky Derby and Preakness Stakes, drew post position two in the seven-horse field and will be ridden by jockey Gary Stevens.
Victory in the Belmont would bring the strapping gray colt a total of $5 million in earnings from the Triple Crown races, including a bonus for sweeping the series.
Silver Charm is trying to become the first horse since Affirmed in 1978 to win the three premier races for three year olds.

The entry of Touch Gold, with jockey Chris McCarron, and Wild Rush, with Jerry Bailey up, is the 2-1 second choice. Touch Gold will break from post position one in the 1 1-2 mile race on Belmont's dirt track. Wild Rush drew post four.
Free House, second to Silver Charm in the Preakness and third in the Derby, is the 5-2 third choice with jockey Kent Desormeaux riding and will break from the sixth post position.
Silver Charm's trainer Bob Baffert showed none of the strain associated with a trainer shooting for the Triple Crown as he smiled his way through the post position draw.
"It's been fun," said Baffert. "There are just a couple of more days left. I'll be glad when it's over. So far, things have gone smoothly. The horse got here great. That's the most important thing."
Baffert was satisfied with Silver Charm's post position.
"I don't think you can have a bad draw with seven horses going a mile and a half," he said about Silver Charms' chances at becoming the 12th horse to win the Triple Crown.
Richard Mandella trainer of Wild Rush, was also in a jocular mood.
"I want to register a complaint," he said. "Bob Baffert is handling that trophy like he's already won it."
Crypto Star, winner of the Louisiana and Illinois derbies, will break from post three under Pat Day and is listed at 6-1.
Mr. Energiser, a 30-1 longshot with Manuel Ortega up, drew post five. Rank outsider Irish Silence, 50-1 with John Velazquez, will break from the seventh position.
Wayne Catalano, trainer of Crypto Star, was pleased his horse would start just outside the favourite.
"I like my post position this time," said Catalano. "I'm looking for a great effort from Crypto Star."
